scope: Only synchronous native integer-record array pointer reads in size/write passes; no public API, wire, ownership or resource budget change.
proofs: Caller is in WireStruct array branch; child binding is native, private int64Record holds and every current nonnegative-tag field passes nativeIntegerFields.

integerRecordPointers requires positive current slice length and actual element type exactly reflect.PointerTo(private child schema.typ); named pointer elements return nil and retain original reflect.Index/UnsafePointer path.

Actual elements are GC pointer slots with native pointer width/alignment; unsafe.Slice reads exactly current Len. Loop indexes stay within the same Len, no uintptr conversion, byte pointer copy or cached addresses.
Each pointer is read for the current element in each pass; nil children are handled by unchanged integer record functions; scalar values still read by unchanged field code.
Message and child graph remain borrowed synchronously and rooted through reflect values/typed pointers and existing runtime.KeepAlive in encodeBufferWithLimits, including preflight failure paths.

Output allocation follows full existing preflight. Same per-element and per-field budgets, depth/tag/byte error ordering, layout growth and final buffer len/cap/nil remain unchanged. No new result buffer, pool, object coalescing or shared mutable output.
costs: One actual-type guard per specialized array per pass and one slot/fallback branch per element; helper and caller code/stack are larger.
Non-target paths can change due to code/register/layout effects; all regressions, controls and cumulative reversals are retained, without attributing all variation to the target branch.
tests: Existing metadata replacement/field shape/nested contracts plus new plain/named slice/named pointer, nil child, current-value, output ownership, exact budget and low GOGC regression. New regression is verified on unmodified baseline first. Full candidate acceptance recorded separately.
limitation: Finite Go1.24.13 darwin/arm64 testing is not a proof of arbitrary future runtime/platform safety. Future layout changes must preserve actual-type proof and synchronous lifetime.
